editorial.headline: Other Hospital Activities: Open Nationally, Address-Specific in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A large-scale hospital activity open to full foreign ownership nationally, with Bali’s moratorium not blocking its medium-high or high-risk classification.
editorial.body:
This activity covers other healthcare and physical-treatment work carried out by hospitals beyond the activity’s more specifically defined hospital categories. Its importance lies in that residual scope: it is intended for hospital-based care and treatment that belongs within the broader hospital setting but is not captured by those defined categories. The classification is therefore not a generic label for every form of health service; its boundary is set by the hospital context and by the care-and-treatment activity described in the record.

The activity is open to businesses at the **Besar** scale. Nationally, it is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical ownership terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. That conclusion rests on the cited national PMA source, Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021, rather than on an implied assumption about healthcare activities generally.

Bali presents a more qualified but still workable picture. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks all low- and medium-low-risk activities island-wide. This activity is not marked as blocked by that moratorium: the Bali record places it in the medium-high or high-risk range and says it is not blocked. For a foreign investor, that is the decisive distinction—the national openness is not overridden here by the Bali moratorium.

There remains one location-specific discipline in the record: the position should be verified for the proposed address. That is not a new restriction or a claim about a permit; it is the stated Bali qualification attached to an activity that remains open nationally and is not moratorium-blocked in Bali. The clear reading is that full foreign ownership is available nationally, while Bali requires the classification to be checked against the actual address before treating the provincial position as settled.
editorial.pullQuote: Full foreign ownership is available nationally, while Bali does not block this activity under its PMA moratorium.
